base_dataset_source: Frey & Osborne (2013). The Future of Employment. University of Oxford.

calibration.rationale: Ghana mobile broadband penetration is approximately 55 per 100 inhabitants (ITU 2024). Low capital intensity and wage levels mean automation of physical-manual tasks is economically unviable for 5-10 years longer than US baseline projections suggest. Routine cognitive tasks (data entry, basic bookkeeping) face faster disruption via mobile AI tools accessible on low-end devices. Social-interactive tasks are less at risk in high-trust informal economies where community relationships drive commerce.

scenario_toggles.label: If technology investment grows fast
scenario_toggles.note: Assumes mobile broadband reaches 80+ per 100 and capital investment accelerates.

scenario_toggles.label: Current infrastructure levels
scenario_toggles.note: Based on current ITU 2024 data for Ghana.

scenario_toggles.label: If technology stays at current levels
scenario_toggles.note: Assumes infrastructure investment stagnates or rural-urban gap widens.

source_label: Frey and Osborne (2013), calibrated for Ghana using ITU 2024 infrastructure data
